root_cause.text: Incorrect error-path cleanup logic in `aml_sfc_dma_buffer_setup()` of the Amlogic SPI Flash Controller driver mishandled DMA mappings by reusing the wrong goto/unmap flow, causing `sfc->daddr` to be unmapped twice and `sfc->iaddr` to be unmapped with the wrong length.
root_cause.evidence: The patch changes the first mapping failure from `goto out_map_data` to `return ret` because “nothing needs cleanup,” removes an inline `dma_unmap_single(sfc->dev, sfc->daddr, datalen, dir);` before `goto out_map_data` to stop double-unmapping, and fixes `out_map_info` from `dma_unmap_single(..., datalen, dir)` to `dma_unmap_single(..., infolen, dir)`.

agent_logs.evidence_points: The patch changes the first mapping failure from `goto out_map_data` to `return ret` because “nothing needs cleanup,” removes an inline `dma_unmap_single(sfc->dev, sfc->daddr, datalen, dir);` before `goto out_map_data` to stop double-unmapping, and fixes `out_map_info` from `dma_unmap_single(..., datalen, dir)` to `dma_unmap_single(..., infolen, dir)`.

intent_record.intent_summary: Return immediately on DMA mapping failure to avoid executing inappropriate cleanup via the out_map_data path.
intent_record.what: The error-handling path after dma_mapping_error() in aml_sfc_dma_buffer_setup() was changed from jumping to the out_map_data label with goto to immediately returning ret.
intent_record.how: When DMA mapping fails, the function now exits directly instead of continuing into the shared cleanup path at out_map_data, preventing any subsequent cleanup or handling tied to that label from running in this failure case.

intent_record.intent_summary: Remove the erroneous DMA unmap on DMA mapping failure to avoid invalid cleanup in the error path.
intent_record.what: The change removes the call to dma_unmap_single(sfc->dev, sfc->daddr, datalen, dir) from the error path immediately after ret = dma_mapping_error(sfc->dev, sfc->iaddr) reports a DMA mapping failure.
intent_record.how: At runtime, when the second DMA mapping check fails, the code no longer attempts to unmap sfc->daddr in that branch, avoiding an unmap operation during a mapping-error path where the mapping may not be valid or should not be released there.

intent_record.intent_summary: Fix the error-path DMA cleanup to unmap the info buffer with infolen instead of the unrelated datalen size.
intent_record.what: The argument passed as the size parameter to dma_unmap_single() in the out_map_info error path was changed from datalen to infolen for the unmapping of sfc->iaddr.
intent_record.how: At runtime, the DMA mapping for the info buffer is now unmapped using the same buffer length that was presumably used when it was mapped, preventing an incorrect DMA unmap size on the error path and avoiding resource handling inconsistencies.

consistency_review.core_intent: Fix the DMA mapping failure error path by avoiding invalid cleanup and returning immediately instead of attempting an erroneous DMA unmap.

The group directly fixes one of the root-cause cleanup bugs in aml_sfc_dma_buffer_setup(): using the correct length (infolen) when unmapping the info buffer instead of the unrelated datalen during the error path.

candidates.rationale: On data DMA mapping failure, this jumps into a cleanup path that unmaps sfc->daddr even though the mapping failed, causing invalid cleanup and contributing to double-unmap behavior.
When info-buffer DMA mapping fails, this explicitly unmaps sfc->daddr and is then followed by a goto to out_map_data, which unmaps sfc->daddr again, directly causing the double unmap.
After already unmapping sfc->daddr on info-buffer mapping failure, this branches to out_map_data where sfc->daddr is unmapped again, completing the double-unmap bug.
This cleanup unmaps the info DMA buffer using datalen instead of infolen, directly matching the root cause of unmapping sfc->iaddr with the wrong length.
This out_map_data cleanup is reached from the erroneous goto paths on mapping failure, so it participates in unmapping sfc->daddr when it should not be unmapped or after it was already unmapped.

vuln_statements.explanation: This error-path cleanup unmaps sfc->daddr during info-buffer DMA mapping failure, and the flow then continues to another cleanup path that unmaps sfc->daddr again, directly causing the double-unmap described in the root cause.

On DMA mapping failure this branches into the out_map_data cleanup path, which performs cleanup intended for a successfully mapped data buffer. That misroutes the error handling and contributes to invalid or repeated unmapping of sfc->daddr.
This statement unmaps the info-buffer DMA address sfc->iaddr using datalen instead of the correct infolen, matching the root cause of cleanup with the wrong length.

bic_trace_step.commit_msg:
spi: amlogic: add driver for Amlogic SPI Flash Controller

This driver provides support for the SPI mode of the Amlogic
bic_trace_step.code_snippet:
commit 4670db6f32e9379f5ab6c9bb2a6787cd9b9230a9
Author: Feng Chen <feng.chen@amlogic.com>
Date:   Wed Sep 10 18:18:26 2025 +0800

    spi: amlogic: add driver for Amlogic SPI Flash Controller
    
    This driver provides support for the SPI mode of the Amlogic
    Flash Controller. It supports both SPI NOR flash and SPI NAND
    flash. For SPI NAND, the Host ECC hardware engine can be enabled.
    
    The controller implements the SPI-MEM interface and does not
    support generic SPI.
bic_trace_step.reason: The vulnerable logic is fully visible in `aml_sfc_dma_buffer_setup()`, so the snippet is sufficient. The function maps `sfc->daddr` first, then optionally maps `sfc->iaddr`. In the error path after info-buffer setup, the code does `out_map_info: dma_unmap_single(sfc->dev, sfc->iaddr, datalen, dir);` and then falls through to `out_map_data: dma_unmap_single(sfc->dev, sfc->daddr, datalen, dir);`. This contains the reported bug for two reasons: (1) `sfc->iaddr` is unmapped with `datalen` instead of `infolen`, which is the wrong length; and (2) in the `if (infobuf)` mapping-failure branch, it already does `dma_unmap_single(sfc->dev, sfc->daddr, datalen, dir);` before `goto out_map_data;`, causing `sfc->daddr` to be unmapped again at `out_map_data`, i.e. a double unmap. Therefore the vulnerable construct is present. The fix is not present because the cleanup labels are still reused incorrectly and there is no corrected separation of cleanup paths using the proper `infolen` for `iaddr` and avoiding a second unmap of `daddr`.
